pieces.file: Leibniz — rich — two clocks, no wire.m4a
pieces.title: Two clocks, no wire
pieces.caption: First, two clocks set once and never touching: a wooden tock in the left ear, a metal tick in the right. They stay together because each keeps its own time. Then a wired pair: they start apart, plainly at different rates, and as the wire tightens they pull into step. Both pairs end in unison. Only the second needed a wire. *What is real and what is a choice:* The first half is Leibniz's pre-established harmony; the second is two Kuramoto phases with rising coupling.
pieces.near: the way two clocks set once keep the same time

pieces.file: Leibniz — rich — every jewel reflects every other.png
pieces.title: Every jewel reflects every other
pieces.caption: The picture at the top of Leibniz's page, rebuilt from the avatars of the other pages. Step back and it is his; step in and it is everyone else's. *What is real and what is a choice:* 1,848 tiles from 123 avatars, each picked for its colour, softened, and tinted most of the way to the colour needed. The tinting is what makes it read. *Leaking in:* Every page in the palace; Indra's Net is the page's own image.
pieces.near: a jewel at every knot reflecting every other jewel
